name: Amperon
product: Cloud software that forecasts electricity demand, renewable generation, prices, and portfolio exposure for utilities and energy-market participants.
targetCustomer: Utilities, energy retailers, generators, traders, and large energy users
buyer: Head of power trading, utility load-forecasting lead, or portfolio-risk leader
traction: The company reports more than 150 customers, coverage of more than 25 grids, and ingestion from more than 40,000 weather locations.
notes: The core is hybrid statistical/ML forecasting rather than a proprietary sensor network; inputs include customer meter or SCADA data plus public and vendor weather feeds. Value depends on clean interval data and integration into trading, scheduling, and utility workflows. Amperon advertises roughly two-week average deployment, but security review and utility procurement can make production rollouts materially longer.

name: Neara
subsector: Utility digital twins and grid planning
product: A physics-enabled digital-twin platform for modeling electric-network assets, terrain, weather exposure, capacity, and failure scenarios.
targetCustomer: Electric utilities and critical-infrastructure owners
buyer: VP of asset management, grid-planning executive, or chief engineer
traction: Neara says its platform models more than 15 million assets across more than two million miles of infrastructure.
notes: The technical center is a physics-based network model augmented by AI, not a generic geospatial dashboard. Deployments require access to asset registries, GIS, LiDAR or imagery, and engineering assumptions; model accuracy inherits errors in those sources. Regulated engineering acceptance, cybersecurity review, and utility procurement create long sales and validation cycles.

name: Camus Energy
product: A grid-management platform that combines distribution visibility, forecasting, flexible-load and DER orchestration, and interconnection workflows.
targetCustomer: Electric distribution utilities and cooperatives
buyer: VP of distribution operations or grid-modernization executive
latestRound: $10M Series A extension; Series A total $26M, 2024
traction: Camus reported a portfolio serving 2.9 million consumers across nine US states and named Duquesne Light, Vermont Electric Cooperative, Kit Carson Electric Cooperative, and La Plata Electric Association as customers in 2024.
notes: This is an operational utility layer rather than a standalone forecast API. It needs AMI, SCADA, GIS, DER telemetry, and often control-system integration; data quality and authority to dispatch customer assets are gating factors. NERC-CIP-adjacent security, regulatory approval, and utility budget cycles can extend sales and deployment.

name: Gridware
product: Pole-mounted sensors plus edge and cloud analytics that detect grid faults, hazards, and wildfire ignition risks on electric distribution networks.
targetCustomer: Electric utilities and public-power operators
buyer: VP of distribution, reliability, or wildfire mitigation
traction: Gridware reported 18 major utility customers in early 2025, including a PG&E expansion to 10,000 poles and 1,000 line miles; later that year it reported 1,700 deployed devices at Duquesne Light.
notes: Pole-level sensing creates a proprietary failure dataset and stronger integration moat than software-only wildfire analytics. It also adds hardware qualification, field installation, maintenance, telecom, and false-alarm burdens. Utility safety cases, regulator scrutiny, rate-recovery processes, and multi-year procurement are the main scaling constraints.

name: Phaidra
product: AI agents that optimize data-center cooling and industrial control systems through supervisory, closed-loop control.
targetCustomer: Hyperscale and colocation data centers and other energy-intensive facilities
buyer: VP of data-center operations, facilities, or infrastructure engineering
traction: Phaidra states that it has deployed supervisory AI controls in data centers, pharmaceutical facilities, and district-energy systems over more than five years.
notes: The defensible work is constrained control built on customer BMS and SCADA telemetry, historical operating data, simulation, and commissioning, not merely the LLM interface. Closed-loop access raises operational-safety, SLA, cyber, and failover requirements. Integration and validation against live facilities make sales cycles long and site-specific.

name: Emerald AI
product: Software that coordinates AI workloads and on-site energy systems so data centers can reduce or shift grid demand while preserving workload service levels.
targetCustomer: AI data-center operators, hyperscalers, and power-constrained compute providers
buyer: Data-center CTO, infrastructure-operations leader, or head of energy
traction: A 2025 field demonstration across 256 GPUs reported a 25% power reduction for three hours while maintaining stated quality-of-service constraints.
notes: Emerald is software-only and early: its field demonstration is useful evidence, but not proof of fleet-scale commercial operation. Production deployment requires scheduler, GPU, telemetry, and possibly battery or generator integration plus auditable workload-SLA controls. Grid-program rules, utility acceptance, and coordination among data-center, compute, and energy teams create multi-party sales cycles.

name: Tyba
product: A battery analytics, forecasting, bidding, and dispatch-optimization platform for storage developers and operators.
targetCustomer: Battery developers, independent power producers, asset owners, and energy traders
buyer: Head of storage asset management or power trading
traction: At the Series A announcement, Tyba reported more than 500 MW of assets under optimization and named TotalEnergies and Intersect Power among customers; a company-hosted report later cited more than 1 GWh in Texas and California.
notes: The product couples ML price forecasts with dispatch constraints, degradation assumptions, and ISO bidding. It relies on site telemetry, market access, and reliable dispatch integration rather than proprietary sensing. Economics are highly market- and rule-specific; battery warranties, ISO certification, and customer risk controls can slow onboarding, and revenue-uplift claims are company-reported.

name: enspired
subsector: Algorithmic energy trading and battery optimization
product: A managed algorithmic trading and optimization service for batteries and other flexible energy assets in European power markets.
targetCustomer: Battery owners, independent power producers, utilities, and flexible-asset operators
buyer: Head of storage asset management, trading, or route-to-market
latestRound: Series B extended to more than EUR 40M, 2025
traction: enspired reported crossing 1 GW of battery capacity in 2025 and later described operations across 12 European countries and roughly 6 GW of flexibility.
notes: This is a vertically integrated route-to-market service, not only SaaS. It combines forecasting, optimization, trading access, and operational responsibility. Grid telemetry, balance-responsible-party arrangements, licensing, collateral, and country-specific market rules are gating inputs; regulatory fragmentation makes expansion operationally heavy and reported performance is not a universal benchmark.

name: Tomorrow.io
product: A weather-intelligence platform combining proprietary satellite observations, external data, AI forecasting, APIs, and operational decision tools.
targetCustomer: Governments and weather-sensitive enterprises in aviation, logistics, insurance, energy, and defense
buyer: Chief operating or risk officer, weather-program lead, or government procurement authority
traction: Tomorrow.io says its first satellite constellation is operational and cites NOAA operational-grade validation among its published milestones.
notes: Owning radar and microwave satellite capacity can create scarce observations, but models also fuse public and third-party weather inputs. The hardware layer introduces launch, constellation-capex, calibration, and coverage risk. Aviation, defense, and government deployments require independent forecast validation, security review, and long procurement; space and spectrum rules add country-specific friction.

name: WindBorne Systems
subsector: Atmospheric sensing and AI weather models
product: A long-duration weather-balloon constellation and AI forecasting stack that supplies proprietary atmospheric observations and global forecasts.
targetCustomer: Government weather agencies and enterprises in energy, aviation, logistics, insurance, and agriculture
buyer: Weather-program director, forecasting lead, or operations-risk executive
traction: WindBorne reports launching hundreds of autonomous balloons per month and has disclosed US government contracts.
notes: The strongest moat is proprietary in-situ atmospheric data generated by low-cost long-duration balloons, paired with AI data assimilation and forecast models. Scaling is exposed to flight permissions, balloon loss, sensing calibration, communications, and geographic coverage. Government procurement is long, and company forecast benchmarks need independent, region- and horizon-specific validation.

name: Climate X
product: Asset-level physical climate-hazard, financial-loss, and adaptation-return analytics for financial institutions and asset owners.
targetCustomer: Banks, insurers, asset managers, real-estate owners, and infrastructure investors
buyer: Chief risk officer, head of climate risk, or portfolio-risk leader
traction: At its Series A, Climate X reported a proprietary database covering 1.5 billion assets and named customers including Legal & General, Federated Hermes, Virgin Money, and CBRE.
notes: Climate X combines physical models and AI, but it is an analytics and decision layer rather than sensing or operational control. Output quality depends on asset geocoding, vulnerability curves, licensed data, and scenario assumptions. Model-risk governance, auditability, evolving disclosure regimes, and integration into underwriting or credit workflows create enterprise-length sales cycles.

name: ZestyAI
product: Property-level wildfire, hail, wind, and structural-risk scores and models used in insurance underwriting, pricing, and portfolio management.
targetCustomer: Property insurers, reinsurers, and public risk programs
buyer: Chief underwriting, pricing, actuarial, or catastrophe-risk executive
traction: ZestyAI reported 31 million property assessments in 2024, 33 new or expanded partnerships, and more than 50 regulatory filings by June 2025.
notes: The moat combines aerial and satellite features, insurer loss data, explainable peril models, and state-by-state regulatory approvals. Insurer datasets and imagery licenses are valuable but costly and access-constrained. Department-of-insurance filings, actuarial validation, core-policy integration, and renewal cycles are both defensibility and a material sales bottleneck.

name: Gigaton
product: Plant-specific digital twins and AI control recommendations that reduce cement-kiln fuel use and process emissions.
targetCustomer: Cement producers and other energy-intensive process manufacturers
buyer: Plant manager, process director, or corporate energy and decarbonization leader
traction: Avant son changement de nom en Gigaton en mai 2026, Carbon Re et ABB avaient annoncé un déploiement exploratoire dans une cimenterie tchèque; il s’agissait d’un protocole d’accord, pas d’une preuve de déploiement à l’échelle d’une flotte.
notes: The technical approach joins thermodynamic models with ML trained on minute-level plant historian data and can sit above existing advanced process control. It does not remove the need for reliable OT data or on-site process engineering. Safety, cybersecurity, control-system integration, production-risk limits, and plant shutdown windows make pilots and sales slow; ABB remains a potential channel rather than a proven scaled route.

sources.label: Carbon Re seed announcement — Gigaton archive

name: Makersite
product: AI and knowledge-graph software that joins product, material, supplier, cost, carbon, and compliance data for engineering and procurement decisions.
targetCustomer: Large manufacturers with complex products and global supply chains
buyer: VP of engineering, procurement, product sustainability, or compliance
traction: Makersite named Microsoft, Daikin, Cummins, Barco, and Schneider Electric as customers and reported a team of more than 150 at its 2025 Series B.
notes: This is a manufacturing analytics and decision layer, not physical process control. Its defensibility is the data foundation and knowledge graph that map incomplete customer BOM, CAD, ERP, and supplier records to external material and impact data. Data licensing, entity quality, PLM/ERP integration, and changing REACH, RoHS, CSRD, and digital-product-passport requirements create both moat and long implementations.

name: KoBold Metals
product: A vertically integrated mineral explorer using geoscience, proprietary field data, sensors, and predictive models to discover and develop critical-mineral deposits.
targetCustomer: KoBold-owned exploration programs, mining joint ventures, and strategic mining partners
buyer: Internal investment committee or mining-company corporate-development and exploration leadership
latestRound: $163.43M sold in a $200M equity offering disclosed in Form D, 2025; follows a reported $537M Series C in 2025
traction: KoBold describes Mingomba in Zambia as its first discovery and is advancing the project with joint-venture partners; discovery does not yet establish an economic reserve or operating mine.
notes: The 5/5 moat reflects vertical ownership of field programs, sensing, subsurface data, modeling, drilling feedback, and mineral rights, not just an exploration algorithm. AI targets do not prove grade, tonnage, recoverability, or economics. Permitting, indigenous and community consent, drilling, feasibility, project finance, commodity prices, and mine development produce years-to-decades cycles.

sources.label: Financial Times Series C report hosted by KoBold

name: Earth AI
product: A vertically integrated mineral-discovery company combining prospect-generation models, field geology, and low-disturbance drilling.
targetCustomer: Earth AI-owned exploration programs and mining or strategic-resource partners
buyer: Internal investment committee or mining-company exploration and corporate-development leadership
traction: Earth AI disclosed an indium-bearing prospect in Australia in 2025; independent reporting emphasized that commercial viability had not yet been demonstrated.
notes: The company closes the loop from model-generated prospects to its own drilling, creating proprietary labels and faster iteration than a software vendor. The score reflects that physical integration, but a mineral indication is not a compliant resource or reserve. Land and mineral rights, cultural and environmental clearances, drilling permits, assays, metallurgy, and development finance dominate timelines.

sources.label: Axios on Earth AI indium prospect

name: Zanskar
product: A full-stack geothermal developer using AI-guided subsurface exploration, field work, drilling, project development, and plant operations.
targetCustomer: Zanskar-owned projects, utilities, corporate power buyers, and infrastructure investors
buyer: Internal project-investment committee, utility or corporate offtaker, and project financier
latestRound: $40M development-capital facility closed, structured to scale to $100M, 2026
traction: Zanskar owns and operates the Lightning Dock geothermal plant and reported multiple field-validated geothermal discoveries before its 2026 Series C.
notes: The 5/5 integration score reflects ownership from exploration models and proprietary field data through drilling, development, and generation assets. It is therefore an infrastructure developer more than a software company. Geology and drilling failure, water and land rights, permitting, transmission interconnection, PPAs, and project finance drive capital intensity and multi-year cycles.

name: AiDASH
product: Satellite and AI software for utility vegetation management, wildfire mitigation, asset inspection, and climate-resilience planning.
targetCustomer: Electric utilities and other linear critical-infrastructure operators
buyer: VP of vegetation management, wildfire mitigation, asset operations, or resilience
traction: AiDASH's strategic investor set includes multiple utilities, and the company has expanded from vegetation management into wildfire, biodiversity, and broader asset-intelligence workflows.
notes: AiDASH primarily turns high-resolution third-party satellite imagery into utility-specific work prioritization; it does not own the sensing constellation. The workflow moat comes from asset models, field feedback, and work-order integration. Utility GIS quality, ground-truth collection, imagery licensing and revisit rates, regulator evidence, and multi-year procurement are key constraints.

name: Overstory
product: Tree-level vegetation, fuel, and wildfire-risk intelligence derived from satellite and aerial imagery for electric-utility operations.
targetCustomer: Electric utilities and vegetation-management contractors
buyer: VP of vegetation management, wildfire mitigation, or grid reliability
traction: Overstory reported serving six of the ten largest electric utilities in the Americas at its 2025 Series B.
notes: Overstory does not own an imagery constellation; differentiation lies in tree- and fuel-level models, accumulated utility labels, and integration into inspection and vegetation-work workflows. Asset GIS, imagery availability, regional species and fire regimes, and field validation affect portability. Regulatory audit requirements and utility procurement make production expansion slower than a normal SaaS sale.

name: OroraTech
product: A thermal-satellite constellation and AI platform for global wildfire detection, monitoring, spread prediction, and response coordination.
targetCustomer: National and regional wildfire agencies, utilities, forestry operators, and insurers
buyer: Wildfire-agency procurement authority, emergency-operations leader, or utility wildfire executive
investors: BNP Paribas Solar Impulse Venture Fund
traction: OroraTech currently reports 14 proprietary satellites, data from more than 35 sources, more than 800 users across 25 countries, and a team exceeding 170.
notes: Unlike imagery-only analytics vendors, OroraTech owns thermal payloads and satellite capacity, creating proprietary low-latency data. That also brings launch, on-orbit calibration, coverage, communications, and false-positive risk. Sovereign procurement, export and space rules, integration into emergency command systems, and proof of detection latency make national deployments long and operationally demanding.
